steps.title: 1990: Iraq invades Kuwait
text: On 2 August 1990 [Iraq](IRQ) invaded and occupied [Kuwait](KWT). A few days later the UN Security Council imposed economic sanctions on Iraq.

In 1991 Kuwait's goods exports fell to **$0.8 billion**, from $8.4 billion in 1990, a year already cut short by the invasion. Iraq's fell to **$0.5 billion**, from $10.3 billion. Fuels made up **95%** of Kuwait's exports in 1995, the first year with product data. The map shows the change in each economy's exports from the year before.

steps.title: Kuwait rebuilds
text: Offensive operations were suspended on 28 February 1991, with Kuwait City liberated. [Kuwait](KWT)'s real GDP shrank **41%** in 1991 and grew 83% in 1992.
By 1993 its exports, $9.0 billion, were back above their 1990 level. The highlighted panel section shows Kuwait's economy in the selected year.

steps.title: Iraq under sanctions
text: [Iraq](IRQ)'s exports stayed at no more than **$0.6 billion** a year from 1991 to 1996. The first Iraqi oil under the UN Oil-for-Food Programme was exported in December 1996, and by 2000 Iraq's exports had reached $15.8 billion, 99.7% of them fuels.
The war that began on 20 March 2003 ended oil exports under the programme. Iraq's real GDP fell **37%** in 2003; its exports reached $16.6 billion in 2004. The lines compare Iraq with [Kuwait](KWT).

steps.title: Libya, 2011
text: On 17 March 2011 the UN Security Council authorized “all necessary measures” to protect civilians in [Libya](LBY) and established a no-fly zone over the country.

Libya's exports, 96% fuels in 2010, fell from $49.2 billion that year to **$18.2 billion** in 2011 (−63%), and its real GDP halved (**−50%**). Exports to [Italy](ITA), its largest customer (26% in 2010), fell from $12.7 billion to $4.4 billion. In 2012 exports rebounded to $56.6 billion.

steps.title: Yemen, since 2015
text: [Yemen](YEM)'s civil war began in 2014, when Houthi insurgents took the capital, Sanaa. From March 2015 a coalition of Gulf states led by [Saudi Arabia](SAU) launched a campaign of economic isolation and air strikes.

Yemen's exports, 90% fuels in 2013, fell from $7.2 billion that year to **$0.4 billion** in 2015, and its real GDP shrank 28% that year. Unlike Kuwait's and Libya's, its exports have not come back: they were $59 million in 2024. The highlighted panel section shows Yemen's trade with the world over time.
